title: Linearity, degree zero, identity and restriction cases of the maps induced by h-maps
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_Y$-module, $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module and $\varphi:\mathcal G\to h_*\mathcal F$ a morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, with $\varphi^*:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ the map of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] and $H^p$ the cohomology of [pqf-def-cohomology], an $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-module (resp. $\mathcal O_X(X)$-module) through the action on the global sections of an injective resolution. (1) (Linearity.) $\varphi^*$ is $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-linear, $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$ acting on $H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ through $h^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y(Y)\to\mathcal O_X(X)$. (2) (Degree zero.) Under the identifications $H^0(Y,\mathcal G)=\mathcal G(Y)$ and $H^0(X,\mathcal F)=\mathcal F(X)$ (a section $s$ goes to the class of its image in the degree-$0$ term of the injective resolution), $\varphi^*$ in degree $0$ is $s\mapsto\varphi_Y(s)\in(h_*\mathcal F)(Y)=\mathcal F(X)$. (3) (Identity.) If $X=Y$, $h=\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, then $\varphi^*=H^p(\varphi)$, the map induced by the functor $H^p(Y,-)$ [pqf-def-cohomology]. (4) (Restriction is a pullback.) For an open $U\subseteq Y$ with inclusion $j:U\to Y$ of the open subscheme, the restriction $\mathrm{res}^Y_U:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(U,\mathcal G|_U)$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b) equals $H^p(\kappa^{-1})\circ j^*$, where $j^*:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(U,j^*\mathcal G)$ is the pullback of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b) and $\kappa:\mathcal G|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*\mathcal G$ is the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] ($\mathcal G|_U$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], $j^*\mathcal G$ as in [def-pc-module-pullback]).

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 01F7 (section-functoriality): Equation 01F9 (equation-functorial-derived, the arrow lives in $D^+(\mathcal O_Y(Y))$, which gives (1)), Equation 01FA (equation-functorial), Lemma 01F8 (lemma-functoriality) with $f=\mathrm{id}$ for (3), Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow); (2) and (4) are not stated in Stacks (statement assembled by the agent; for (4) see also literature/stacks-project/sheaves.tex Lemma 00A0, lemma-j-pullback)

proof.text: *Set-up: the identifications and the module structures.* $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ have enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], and $H^p(Y,-)$ is the $p$-th right derived functor of the additive functor $\Gamma(Y,-)$ on $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ [pqf-def-cohomology]. So [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] (with $v=\Gamma(Y,-)$) gives, for every injective resolution $s_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ with $\mathcal J^n=0$ for $n<0$, an isomorphism $\iota_{\mathcal J}:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^\bullet))$, and for every morphism $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G_1$, every such resolution $\mathcal G_1\to\mathcal J_1^\bullet$ and every morphism of complexes $t:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J_1^\bullet$ with $t^0s_{\mathcal G}=s_{\mathcal G_1}u$ one has $H^p(u)=\iota_{\mathcal J_1}^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,t))\iota_{\mathcal J}$; likewise on $X$. The identifications $H^p(Y,\mathcal G)=H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^\bullet))$, $H^p(X,\mathcal F)=H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] are $\iota_{\mathcal J}$, $\iota_{\mathcal I}$, so for the choices $(\mathcal I^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet,\mathcal J'^\bullet,\lambda,\beta)$ of that definition $\varphi^*=\iota_{\mathcal I}^{-1}\circ H^p(\mu)^{-1}\circ H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta))\circ\iota_{\mathcal J}$ with $\mu=\Gamma(Y,\lambda)$. The module structure of the statement: each $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^n)=\mathcal J^n(Y)$ is an $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-module and the differentials $d^n_Y$ are $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-linear (components of morphisms of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]), so cycles, boundaries and $H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^\bullet))$ are $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-modules, and $H^p(Y,\mathcal G)$ gets the structure transported by $\iota_{\mathcal J}$. It does not depend on $\mathcal J^\bullet$: for a second resolution $\mathcal G\to\mathcal J_2^\bullet$, [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] (applied to the augmentation $\mathcal G[0]\to\mathcal J^\bullet$, a termwise monomorphism and quasi-isomorphism, and to $s_{\mathcal G_2}:\mathcal G[0]\to\mathcal J_2^\bullet$) gives $t:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J_2^\bullet$ with $t^0s_{\mathcal G}=s_{\mathcal G_2}$, and the displayed formula for $u=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G}$ ($H^p(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$, $H^p(Y,-)$ being a functor) gives $\iota_{\mathcal J_2}=H^p(\Gamma(Y,t))\circ\iota_{\mathcal J}$, where $H^p(\Gamma(Y,t))$ is $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-linear because every $t^n_Y$ is. The same holds on $X$ with $\mathcal O_X(X)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow): 'The complex on the bottom left represents $R\Gamma(Y,\mathcal G)$ and the complex on the top right represents $R\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$'; Equation 01F9 (equation-functorial-derived) places the arrow in $D^+(\mathcal O_Y(Y))$; comparison of resolutions: literature/stacks-project/derived.tex Lemma 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift)

proof.text: *Clause (1), linearity.* Fix choices as in Step 1. For $a\in\mathcal O_Y(Y)$: $\Gamma(Y,\beta^n)=\beta^n_Y:\mathcal J^n(Y)\to\mathcal J'^n(Y)$ is $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-linear ($\beta^n$ a morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]); $\mu^n=\lambda^n_Y:(h_*\mathcal I^n)(Y)\to\mathcal J'^n(Y)$ is $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-linear, and $(h_*\mathcal I^n)(Y)=\mathcal I^n(X)$ with $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$ acting through $h^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y(Y)\to\mathcal O_X(h^{-1}Y)=\mathcal O_X(X)$, which is how the direct image of an $\mathcal O_X$-module is an $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-pc-module-pullback]. A linear morphism of complexes induces linear maps on $H^p$, and the inverse of a bijective linear map is linear; $H^p(\mu)$ is bijective [lem-weil-pbc-module-pushforward-injectives-sections-quasi-iso]. Hence $H^p(\mu)^{-1}\circ H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta))$ is $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-linear from $H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^\bullet))$ to $H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$, the latter an $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-module through $h^\sharp$ (restriction of scalars of its $\mathcal O_X(X)$-structure), and $\iota_{\mathcal J}$, $\iota_{\mathcal I}$ are linear by the definition of the module structures (Step 1); so $\varphi^*$ is $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-linear.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Equation 01F9 (equation-functorial-derived): the arrow $R\Gamma(Y,\mathcal G)\to R\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ lives in $D^+(\mathcal O_Y(Y))$; Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow): both arrows of the second diagram are $\Gamma(Y,-)$ of maps of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules

proof.text: *Clause (2), degree zero.* $\Gamma(Y,-)$ is additive and preserves kernels (kernels in $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]), so it is left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (2) the map $\mathcal G(Y)\to H^0(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^\bullet))=\ker(d^0_Y)$, $s\mapsto[s_{\mathcal G}(s)]$, is an isomorphism (since $\mathcal J^{-1}=0$, $H^0$ is the group of $0$-cycles); likewise $\mathcal F(X)\cong H^0(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$, $t\mapsto[s_{\mathcal F}(t)]$. These are the identifications of the statement (composed with $\iota^{-1}$; by Step 1 a change of resolution $t:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J_2^\bullet$ sends $[s_{\mathcal G}(s)]$ to $[t^0s_{\mathcal G}(s)]=[s_{\mathcal G_2}(s)]$, so they do not depend on the resolution). Let $s\in\mathcal G(Y)$ and $t=\varphi_Y(s)\in(h_*\mathcal F)(Y)=\mathcal F(h^{-1}Y)=\mathcal F(X)$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. The element $s_{\mathcal F,X}(t)\in\mathcal I^0(X)$ is a $0$-cycle ($d^0s_{\mathcal F}=0$), and, since $(h_*s_{\mathcal F})_Y=s_{\mathcal F,X}$ and $\mu^0=\lambda^0_Y$, $\mu^0(s_{\mathcal F,X}(t))=(\lambda^0\circ h_*(s_{\mathcal F})\circ\varphi)_Y(s)=(\beta^0\circ s_{\mathcal G})_Y(s)=\beta^0_Y(s_{\mathcal G,Y}(s))$ by the defining equation of $\beta$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. So $H^0(\mu)[s_{\mathcal F}(t)]=H^0(\Gamma(Y,\beta))[s_{\mathcal G}(s)]$, i.e. $H^0(\mu)^{-1}H^0(\Gamma(Y,\beta))[s_{\mathcal G}(s)]=[s_{\mathcal F}(\varphi_Y(s))]$: under the identifications, $\varphi^*$ in degree $0$ is $s\mapsto\varphi_Y(s)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow), the commutative square (equation-choice) read in degree $0$ on global sections; not stated in Stacks, computation written by the agent

proof.text: *Clause (3), the identity case.* Let $X=Y$, $h=\mathrm{id}_Y$; then $h_*$ is the identity functor of $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ ($(h_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V)$, $h^\sharp=\mathrm{id}$ [def-pc-module-pullback]) and $\mu=\Gamma(Y,\lambda)$. Take any choices $(\mathcal I^\bullet,s_{\mathcal F})$, $(\mathcal J^\bullet,s_{\mathcal G})$, $\lambda:\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$, $\beta$ with $\beta^0s_{\mathcal G}=\lambda^0s_{\mathcal F}\varphi$ as in [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. The augmentation $\alpha:\mathcal G[0]\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ is a termwise monomorphism and a quasi-isomorphism, and $s_{\mathcal F}\varphi:\mathcal G[0]\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a morphism of complexes ($d^0s_{\mathcal F}=0$) into a bounded below complex of injectives; by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] there is $\gamma:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ with $\gamma^0s_{\mathcal G}=s_{\mathcal F}\varphi$. Then $\lambda\gamma$ and $\beta:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ satisfy $(\lambda\gamma)\alpha=\beta\alpha$ (both are $\lambda^0s_{\mathcal F}\varphi$ in degree $0$), and $\mathcal J'^\bullet$ is a bounded below complex of injectives, so $\lambda\gamma$ and $\beta$ are chain-homotopic [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy]. The additive functor $\Gamma(Y,-)$ carries a homotopy $k$ to the homotopy $\Gamma(Y,k)$, and homotopic morphisms induce the same map on $H^p$; so $H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta))=H^p(\mu)\circ H^p(\Gamma(Y,\gamma))$ and, by Step 1, $\varphi^*=\iota_{\mathcal I}^{-1}H^p(\mu)^{-1}H^p(\mu)H^p(\Gamma(Y,\gamma))\iota_{\mathcal J}=\iota_{\mathcal I}^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\gamma))\iota_{\mathcal J}=H^p(\varphi)$, the last equality by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] applied to $\varphi$ and the lift $\gamma$ ($\gamma^0s_{\mathcal G}=s_{\mathcal F}\varphi$). This holds for every choice of the data, so no independence statement is needed.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma 01F8 (lemma-functoriality) and Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow) with $f=\mathrm{id}$; literature/stacks-project/derived.tex Lemma 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift) and Lemma 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy)

proof.text: *Clause (4), the two $j$-maps and a common resolution on $Y$.* Let $\rho=\rho_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to j_*(\mathcal G|_U)$ (on $V\subseteq Y$ the restriction $\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal G(V\cap U)$) and $\eta:\mathcal G\to j_*j^*\mathcal G$ the unit, so $\mathrm{res}^Y_U=\rho^*$ and $j^*=\eta^*$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (a),(b). The unit of $(-)|_U\dashv j_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] is, on $V\subseteq Y$, the restriction $\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal G(j(j^{-1}V))=\mathcal G(V\cap U)$, i.e. it is $\rho$, so that lemma gives $j_*(\kappa)\circ\rho=\eta$, i.e. $\rho=j_*(\kappa^{-1})\circ\eta$ and $\eta=j_*(\kappa)\circ\rho$. Fix choices for $\rho^*$: $(\mathcal J^\bullet,s_{\mathcal G})$ on $Y$, an injective resolution $s_{\mathcal I}:\mathcal G|_U\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, $\lambda:j_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$, $\beta$ with $\beta^0s_{\mathcal G}=\lambda^0j_*(s_{\mathcal I})\rho$, $\mu=\Gamma(Y,\lambda)$; and for $\eta^*$: $(\mathcal J_2^\bullet,s_2)$ on $Y$, $s':j^*\mathcal G\to\mathcal I'^\bullet$, $\lambda':j_*\mathcal I'^\bullet\to\mathcal J''^\bullet$, $\beta'$ with $\beta'^0s_2=\lambda'^0j_*(s')\eta$, $\mu'=\Gamma(Y,\lambda')$. As in Step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] gives $t:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J_2^\bullet$ with $t^0s_{\mathcal G}=s_2$ and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] (with $u=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G}$) gives $\iota_{\mathcal J_2}=H^p(\Gamma(Y,t))\iota_{\mathcal J}$. Put $\beta''=\beta't:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J''^\bullet$; then $\beta''^0s_{\mathcal G}=\beta'^0s_2=\lambda'^0j_*(s')\eta$ and $j^*=\iota_{\mathcal I'}^{-1}H^p(\mu')^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta'))\iota_{\mathcal J_2}=\iota_{\mathcal I'}^{-1}H^p(\mu')^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta''))\iota_{\mathcal J}$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00A0 (lemma-j-pullback): $j^{-1}\mathcal G=\mathcal G|_U$ for an open immersion; literature/stacks-project/cohomology.tex Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow) for the data; clause (4) is not stated in Stacks, argument written by the agent

proof.text: *Clause (4), comparing the resolutions on $U$ and the complexes $\mathcal J'',\mathcal J'$.* The augmentation $j^*\mathcal G[0]\to\mathcal I'^\bullet$ is a termwise monomorphism and a quasi-isomorphism and $s_{\mathcal I}\kappa^{-1}:j^*\mathcal G[0]\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a morphism of complexes into a bounded below complex of injective $\mathcal O_U$-modules, so [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] gives $c:\mathcal I'^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ with $c^0s'=s_{\mathcal I}\kappa^{-1}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] (for $v=\Gamma(U,-)$ on $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, which has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]) gives $H^p(\kappa^{-1})=\iota_{\mathcal I}^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(U,c))\iota_{\mathcal I'}$. Next, $\mathcal J'^\bullet$ is a bounded below complex of injectives, so every morphism from an acyclic complex to it is null-homotopic [lem-weil-pbc-acyclic-map-to-injective-nullhomotopy]; by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] the localization $Q$ to the derived category of $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ induces bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(N,\mathcal J'^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(QN,Q\mathcal J'^\bullet)$ for every complex $N$. Since $Q(\lambda')$ is an isomorphism ($\lambda'$ is a quasi-isomorphism), precomposition with $\lambda'$, $\operatorname{Hom}_K(\mathcal J''^\bullet,\mathcal J'^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Hom}_K(j_*\mathcal I'^\bullet,\mathcal J'^\bullet)$, corresponds under these bijections to precomposition with $Q(\lambda')$ and is bijective. Hence there is a morphism of complexes $e:\mathcal J''^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ with $e\lambda'$ chain-homotopic to $\lambda\circ j_*(c)$ ($j_*(c)$ is a morphism of complexes, $j_*$ being additive [def-pc-module-pullback]). Applying the additive functor $\Gamma(Y,-)$ (which preserves homotopies) and $H^p$, and using $\Gamma(Y,j_*(c))=c_{j^{-1}Y}=\Gamma(U,c)$ under $\Gamma(Y,j_*\mathcal I^n)=\mathcal I^n(U)$ [def-pc-module-pullback]: $H^p(\Gamma(Y,e))\circ H^p(\mu')=H^p(\mu)\circ H^p(\Gamma(U,c))$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 05TG (lemma-morphisms-into-injective-complex): $\Mor_{K(\mathcal A)}(L^\bullet,I^\bullet)=\Mor_{D(\mathcal A)}(L^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ for $I^\bullet$ bounded below of injectives; Lemma 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift)

proof.text: *Clause (4), $e\beta''$ is homotopic to $\beta$.* With $\alpha:\mathcal G[0]\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ the augmentation (a quasi-isomorphism), $\beta''\alpha=\lambda'\circ j_*(s')\circ\eta$ and $\beta\alpha=\lambda\circ j_*(s_{\mathcal I})\circ\rho$ as morphisms $\mathcal G[0]\to\mathcal J''^\bullet$, resp. $\mathcal J'^\bullet$ (Step 5; here $s'$, $s_{\mathcal I}$ are viewed as morphisms of complexes from the modules in degree $0$). Composition preserves homotopy, so by Step 6 $e\beta''\alpha=(e\lambda')j_*(s')\eta$ is homotopic to $\lambda j_*(c)j_*(s')\eta=\lambda j_*(c^0s')\eta=\lambda j_*(s_{\mathcal I})j_*(\kappa^{-1})\eta=\lambda j_*(s_{\mathcal I})\rho=\beta\alpha$, using $c^0s'=s_{\mathcal I}\kappa^{-1}$ (Step 6) and $j_*(\kappa^{-1})\eta=\rho$ (Step 5). Since $\mathcal J'^\bullet$ is a bounded below complex of injectives and $\alpha$ a quasi-isomorphism, [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy] gives that $e\beta''$ and $\beta$ are chain-homotopic; hence $H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta))=H^p(\Gamma(Y,e))\circ H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta''))$.

*Clause (4), conclusion.* $H^p(\mu)$ and $H^p(\mu')$ are bijective [lem-weil-pbc-module-pushforward-injectives-sections-quasi-iso]; multiplying the identity of Step 6 by $H^p(\mu)^{-1}$ on the left and $H^p(\mu')^{-1}$ on the right gives $H^p(\mu)^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,e))=H^p(\Gamma(U,c))H^p(\mu')^{-1}$. With Steps 1, 5 and 7: $\mathrm{res}^Y_U=\rho^*=\iota_{\mathcal I}^{-1}H^p(\mu)^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta))\iota_{\mathcal J}=\iota_{\mathcal I}^{-1}H^p(\mu)^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,e))H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta''))\iota_{\mathcal J}=\iota_{\mathcal I}^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(U,c))H^p(\mu')^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta''))\iota_{\mathcal J}=\bigl(\iota_{\mathcal I}^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(U,c))\iota_{\mathcal I'}\bigr)\circ\bigl(\iota_{\mathcal I'}^{-1}H^p(\mu')^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta''))\iota_{\mathcal J}\bigr)=H^p(\kappa^{-1})\circ j^*$, for every choice of the data of both maps.
